A dim, damp underground chamber. There is none of the splendor of a Kazimierz arena here—only the smell of blood and the snarling of a beast.
A lavishly dressed man watched with satisfaction through the iron cage as the enormous beast, freshly injected with a serum, hurled itself against the bars in a frenzy.
'Yes, yes... that's the kind of rage I want! I've got three million riding on tomorrow's match, so you'd better tear that thing to pieces for me! Hahahaha!'
Clack. The heavy metal door was pushed open.
The man whipped around in alarm. 'Who's there?!'
A Kuranta woman walked in, a shield slung across her back and a sword hanging from one hand, for all the world like a knight.
'Which order are you from? I've never seen you before!' shouted the man, all bluster and no spine. 'Get out! This is no place for you!'
The Kuranta woman came at last to a halt.
'I heard there was a formidable beast down here. I've come to challenge it.'
'Ha? Challenge it?' The man laughed as though he had heard the joke of the century—and then he took in her gear. 'Who do you think you are? The Blood Knight? The Radiant Knight? Get lost, or my guards—'
Several guards lunged out of the shadows. At that instant a volley of arrows came flying out of their blind spot, cutting their movements short with perfect precision, and then a flippant-looking Sarkaz man and a shield-bearing Reproba came charging out of the dark and pinned the guards down without effort.
And out of the Kuranta woman's comms terminal came a young girl's voice: 'Big sis Catapult, I've got the entrance covered, nobody's getting in!'
The man had no time even to scream before that shield slammed into his chest and pressed him flat against the wall, and he was out cold in an instant.
She turned to face the beast, still roaring wildly and trying to get at her. She seemed long since used to scenes like this—she was even in the mood to tease the figures in the darkness. 'Oh my, big sis Orchid. What are you all doing here?'
The Liberi woman with the bow stepped out of the shadows and rolled her eyes. 'So you're telling me you 'left' your plan lying on the table that obviously, and then expected me not to follow once I'd seen it? Don't take everything you wanted and then act innocent about it.'
'Heheh.' The Kuranta woman rubbed her nose happily. Of course she had done it on purpose. That was her method—her method for dragging everyone in A6 into her 'hunting business.'
'Seriously, could you not pick a slightly easier target for once?' the Liberi woman could not help grumbling, hunching her shoulders. The dank chill of the place really did not agree with her.
'Can't be helped,' the Kuranta woman shrugged. 'It's hardly my fault that the fiercest beasts on this land aren't the ones with the fangs and claws.'
With that, she opened the door of the cage, and the other three fell in behind her as a matter of course.
'Let's make it quick. It's nearly Popukar's bedtime.'
